thread:
maria: heads-up — after the kernel-selection tweak landed on canary we saw a host-side p99 decode bump (~12-18%).
ajay: is that GPU or host CPU?
maria: host CPU. traces point at tokenization + request parse path, specifically streaming chunk boundary handling.
lucy: any KV cache impact?
maria: yes. kvcache hit rate dropped ~6% for a subset of traffic. keys look identical except boundary offsets changed.
otto: can you paste the perf output?
maria: sure. snippet from perf top during a repro window:
```
Samples: 1K of event 'cycles'
  24.3%  runtime:parse_stream_chunk
  17.9%  runtime:tokenize_utf8
  12.4%  libc-2.31.so:memcpy
   9.7%  runtime:handle_grpc_headers
   6.1%  runtime:kvcache_lookup
```
ajay: memcpy being that high smells like extra copying on frame reassembly. we changed the kernel selector to prefer narrow-kernel layouts for short sequences — might be producing more fragmented host frames.
natalie: I also pulled a tcpdump/har of a sample request, see the framing pattern: lots of 64-128B fragments instead of single 512B. that increases reassembly cost.
lucy: streaming gRPC + http2 small frames -> more writev/readv opportunities. are we still coalescing iovecs?
maria: our proxy path falls back to a buffer-copy if chunk count > 8. with the kernel change the typical chunk count crossed that threshold.
otto: ok. two knobs: 1) raise iovec threshold to avoid copies, 2) change the chunker to prefer coalescing small inbound frames into a single buffer sooner.
ajay: but raising threshold blindly could increase tail latency under heavy concurrency. need canary.
perf-bot: benchmark run complete — baseline vs canary (1000 reqs)
perf-bot: baseline p99=48ms, canary p99=54ms, avg CPU usage host +11%
maria: repro command used:
```bash
./bench --concurrency 128 --payload 1kb --streaming=true --frames=rand(64,128)
```
lucy: also saw kvcache thrash: hot shard saw 3x eviction churn. because tokenization boundaries change, bloom/key prefix mismatch.
oto: (typo) otto: we should normalize keys using canonical token boundaries before hashing into the cache. that would decouple kvcache keys from micro-boundary shifts.
natalie: agree but normalization adds CPU. maybe instead stash a short prefix canonicalizer that only runs on misses, not every lookup.
ajay: good idea — do prefix canonicalization on miss path and seed cache with canonical key. cheap for hit path.
maria: I put a quick patch in a fork that: (a) coalesces small frames earlier, (b) increases iov threshold from 8->12, (c) kvcache miss-prefix-normalize. microbench on my laptop showed p99 back to 49ms, host CPU +3% (vs +11%).
lucy: can we see the diff?
maria: diff gist:```diff
--- a/proxy/ingress/chunker.go
+++ b/proxy/ingress/chunker.go
@@ -102,7 +102,9 @@ func coalesce(iovs []iovec) []byte {
-    if len(iovs) > 8 { return copyAndJoin(iovs) }
+    // bump threshold to prefer writev when we can 
+    if len(iovs) > 12 { return copyAndJoin(iovs) }
+    // also try fast coalesce for sub-256B frames
     return joinFast(iovs)
 }
```
ote: it's intentionally small and guarded.
perf-bot: quick canary run on canary-2 -> p99=50ms, kvcache hit restored +4%, host CPU +4%
deploy-bot: Canary deploy rolled out at 6501112300 to canary-2
ajay: good. two followups: 1) formalize key canonicalizer (perf test under high qps), 2) add unit test to chunker to avoid future regressions.
maria: opened issue #1234 with the trace, perf table, and patch link. assigning to @ajay for canonicalizer and @lucy for chunker tests.
otto: I'll watch kvcache telemetry for the next 24h and alert if eviction spikes >2x.
natalie: let's also add a quick e2e bench to CI that hits streaming small-frame mix so this doesn't slip.
ajay: agree. i'll land the guarded patch to canary-2, schedule the canonicalizer work next sprint.
maria: thanks all. summary: kernel-selection change exposed a coupling between chunking heuristics and kvcache keying; mitigations (coalesce earlier + miss-path canonicalization) restore p99 and limit CPU regression.
lucy: :thumbsup:
